angles.drive: Your own standard is the only one you answer to. Your Metal runs deep, so a line you drew once stays drawn without effort. You hold it because it is right, or you hold it because bending would feel like losing yourself. The price is company that can match you, which is rare.

angles.cost_self: You keep your own counsel, and it looks free. Metal runs over in you, so the surface holds. You stay quiet because the trouble is yours to carry, or because being carried would mean being seen. No one gets asked when you are in trouble. You pay for that by being alone with it.

angles.drive: Letting people in stopped being something you decline and became something you cannot quite locate. Fine, you say, on the day of the diagnosis, the layoff, the breakup. The word has three hundred uses now, and not one of them means fine.

angles.cost_self: A friend was in town for one evening, the first in three years. Lights out at eleven held anyway, the way it held through the fever, the way it holds through everything. You slept on schedule and lay there knowing exactly what the schedule had cost.

ledger: the Twin's standard held to oneself: the line that will not bend, priced in matching company
the Twin's self-reliance that walls others out: counsel kept, trouble carried alone
